title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 160
paragraphs: This Battus had a son named Arcesilaus who, on becoming king, quarreled with his own brothers until in the end they left for another region of Libya and, acting on their own initiative, founded the city that then and now is called Barca; and at the same time as they founded it, they induced the Libyans to revolt from the Cyrenaeans. After this, Arcesilaus led an expedition against those Libyans who had received his brothers and had also revolted from Cyrene. The Libyans, afraid of him, fled toward the eastern tribes of Libyans; and Arcesilaus pursued them as they fled, until in his pursuit he reached Leucon in Libya. There the Libyans resolved to make a stand. They joined battle and defeated the Cyrenaeans so decisively that seven thousand Cyrenaean hoplites fell on that field. After this disaster, Arcesilaus, being sick and having swallowed a potion, was strangled by his brother Haliarchus; and Haliarchus was killed by treachery by Arcesilaus's wife, whose name was Eryxo.
